commits.message:
fix(tree): a node's style draws its row and every row beneath it (rich-tree-736)

Tree stored `style` and never read it. The walk now stacks each node's
style the way it already stacked guide styles; the label is drawn over it,
so its own markup still wins, and only its background reaches the guides,
as in Rich. docs/tree.md gets its style example back.

fix(markdown): every option takes effect or is gone (rich-markdown-ft8) (#259)

* fix(markdown): every option takes effect or is gone (rich-markdown-ft8)

- inlineCodeStyle styles inline code (was hard-coded to markdown.code).
- hyperlinks: true makes a link's text the link, in markdown.link_url;
  false draws the text in markdown.link and writes " (url)" after it, as
  Rich does.
- justify places paragraphs, list items and quoted text; headings keep
  their own placement. It was declared and never read, same defect.
- codeTheme is removed: Syntax lost its theme option in #256, colours are
  console theme names, so there is nothing for it to name.

* fix(markdown): links span their text, headings stay left, justify has one source (rich-markdown-ft8)

Review round 1 (high) on #259:
- a link's span starts where its text lands, not at the source length, which
  control-character stripping can shorten
- headings are placed left explicitly instead of inheriting the print's justify
- justify travels once, as the block's placement; InlineSettings holds only
  inline code style and hyperlinks, and Markdown no longer implements it
- docs: an unset justify follows the print's

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(markdown): a heading is drawn at its natural width (rich-markdown-ft8)

Review round 2 (medium) on #259: placing headings "left" padded them to the
width, and markdown.h1's underline ran to the edge. A heading now renders
with no placement asked of it, so the print's justify cannot reach it either.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(markdown): body text defaults to left, as Rich's Paragraph does (rich-markdown-ft8)

Review round 3 (escalation high) on #259: Rich's Paragraph uses
markdown.justify or "left", so an unset justify never inherits the print's.
The settings object carries justify once, and the Justify type derives from
RenderOptions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
